quarterly_data.quarter: UMS Integration press release: UMS net profit soars 90% to $19.8m on higher revenue (08-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2QFY2026 / 1HFY2026 results: 2Q revenue S$87.1 million (+29% YoY, +26% QoQ), net profit S$19.8 million (+90%), net attributable profit S$19.4 million; semiconductor revenue S$75.5 million (+28%), with integrated-system sales S$33.5 million (+19%) and component sales S$42.1 million (+37%); aerospace S$8.6 million (+59%). 1H revenue S$156.5 million (+25%), net attributable profit S$33.4 million (+66%), semiconductor S$134.5 million (+25%). Malaysia revenue rose 50% to S$14.0 million in 2Q as it ramped semiconductor component production for its new major customer (not named), and Korea revenue rose 347% to S$6.4 million on shipments to that customer's location in Korea. Gross material margin 54.2% in 2Q. 1H capex S$9.6 million, mainly for the Penang expansion; during 2Q it repaid the loan taken for its acquisition of the remaining 30% minority interest in Starke Singapore. CEO Andy Luong: current performance does not yet reflect the full contribution of several new manufacturing services being set up and qualified, and key customers have given strong equipment-demand forecasts for several years ahead.
quarterly_data.figure: 2QFY2026 revenue S$87.1 million (+29% YoY); net profit S$19.8 million (+90%); 1H revenue S$156.5 million (+25%)

quarterly_data.quarter: UMS Integration press release: UMS net profit soars 90% to $19.8m on higher revenue (08-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and outlook (2QFY2026 release): given tight near-term capacity in the semiconductor components supply chain, UMS is expanding its footprint - on June 4, 2026 it signed a non-binding MoU on a proposed investment in Vietnam-based precision engineering, metal processing and plating businesses to add capacity and ease tight labour in Malaysia - and is working on its new major customer's new-product-introduction programme to complete qualification and ramp programmes. Both its major customers have projected year-on-year demand growth in 2026 and 2027. Barring unforeseen circumstances, the group expects to remain profitable in FY2026. CEO Andy Luong: with new production facilities in Malaysia and Vietnam it is equipped to support customers' growth in leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM memory and advanced packaging tied to AI infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: Vietnam capacity MoU signed June 4, 2026; major customers project growth in 2026 and 2027
